newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan report finds Peru embassy lapse - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Japan report finds Peru embassy lapse - newspaper.

text.p: A Foreign Ministry review of the Lima hostage crisis has found Tokyo's embassy failed to gather enough intelligence about the possibility of an attack on the ambassador's residence, a Japanese daily reported on Sunday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said a Foreign Ministry report, to be submitted to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda this week, found the intelligence lapse left security "blind spots."

"While it is not appropriate to take issue with the hosting of a reception to celebrate the Emperor's birthday, the amount of information that the diplomatic staff obtained beforehand was insufficient," the Nihon Keizai quoted the report as saying.
"This led to blind spots in the security arrangement, most notably in the absence of an officer standing guard at the back of the residence," the report said.

Fourteen Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the reception on December 17, taking hundreds of VIP hostages and held out against security forces for 127 days in Latin America's longest ever siege drama.
Peruvian troops stormed the residence on April 23, killing all the MRTA guerrillas and rescuing alive all but one of the remaining 72 hostages.

The report says Japanese diplomats in Lima did not maintain adequate contacts with Peruvian intelligence sources after being reassured by President Alberto Fujimori that the MRTA was no longer a threat, the Nihon Keizai said.
After receiving the report, Hashimoto and Ikeda will decide on possible disciplinary measures, the newspaper said.
Japan's ambassador to Peru Morihisa Aoki, who was a hostage throughout the siege, has already resigned over the affair.
